Specify an age-specific fertility process

Source: R/fertility.R
fertility.Rd

Constructs a fertility process specification for a simulation model. The convenience function set_fertility is equivalent to set_process(model, fertility(...)) and allows for direct piping from a model.

Usage

fertility(rates, birth_interval = 0.75, ffab = 0.4886, weights = NULL)

set_fertility(
  model,
  rates,
  birth_interval = 0.75,
  ffab = 0.4886,
  weights = NULL
)

Arguments

rates

A nonempty data frame defining the fertility rate schedules. Must contain at least numeric age_start, age_end, and rate. See details for description of stratification variables that can be applied.

birth_interval

Minimum maternal birth-to-birth interval in years, defaulting to 0.75. Must be finite and nonnegative.

ffab

Probability that a newborn is female, default 0.4886. Must be a finite numeric scalar between 0 and 1.

weights

NULL (default) for unweighted selection within rate cells, or a weight_model() specification. Weights choose which member of a cell experiences an event without changing the cell's input rate.

model

A hammel_model object, used by set_fertility().

Value

fertility() returns an inspectable process inheriting from hammel_fertility and hammel_process, with name, rates, birth_interval, ffab, and weights. set_fertility() returns an updated hammel_model.

Details

The primary and only required input to the function is a fertility rate schedule for the rates argument. This data frame must contain age_start and age_end columns to define the half-open age intervals (inclusive at the start and exclusive at the end) and a rate column for the age-specific fertility rates. The example below shows the basic format:

#> # A tibble: 6 x 3
#>   age_start age_end   rate
#>       <int>   <int>  <dbl>
#> 1        15      20 0.0477
#> 2        20      25 0.110
#> 3        25      30 0.114
#> 4        30      35 0.0912
#> 5        35      40 0.0397
#> 6        40      45 0.008

Rates are always specified as births over person-years lived for women. An open-ended age group specified with age_end of Inf can be included but is not required. Any age groups without a specified rate will be assumed to have a zero rate.

Columns named by declared group dimensions (see set_groups()), such as race or region, supply separate schedules for each combination of their categories; dimensions without a column share the schedule. Every combination of categories of the dimensions must be included in the rates if the dimension is used.

Optional time_start/time_end columns select half-open calendar intervals in absolute years, including fractional years. Both columns are required together; starts are finite and ends exceed starts (possibly Inf). Active slices must satisfy the strata and coverage rules and cover the requested simulation run.

Fertility optionally accepts union_type containing both "partnered" and "unpartnered", or all three of "unpartnered", "cohab", "marriage". Shared partnered rates cover either partnership type. Rates use woman-years in the indicated type; the old fertility input union_status is rejected. Without that column, one overall schedule applies to all women. On-demand union formation requires overall rates; rate-based formation accepts either form, but using overall fertility rates with specified union formation rates will lead to independence between marriage and fertility, which is likely undesirable in most applications. A warning is printed if this is the case.

Optional parity_start/parity_end use half-open current maternal parity bands, covering zero through Inf without gaps or overlap in every group/type stratum.

The stratify_rates() function provides a quick means to add stratification to an existing rate schedule.

See also

set_process(), mortality(), union_formation(), group_inheritance()

Examples

fert_process <- fertility(usa_2000_fertility)
model <- hammel_model() |> set_process(fert_process)
# Equivalent convenience setter:
model <- hammel_model() |> set_fertility(usa_2000_fertility)
